facts.statement: Dollosuchoides is an extinct genus of gavialoid crocodilian known colloquially as the Crocodile of Maransart.
facts.quote: Dollosuchoides, colloquially known as the Crocodile of Maransart, is an extinct monospecific genus of gavialoid crocodilian

facts.statement: The holotype specimen IRScNB 482 was discovered in 1915 and prepared between 1926 and 1927 by Hubert, Mehschaert, and Jean de Kleermaeker.
facts.quote: The holotype, IRScNB 482, was discovered in 1915 and it was prepared during 1926–1927 by M. Hubert, J. Mehschaert and M. Jean de Kleermaeker

facts.statement: Louis Dollo intended to describe the holotype in 1931 but died before he could publish the description.
facts.quote: Louis Dollo had the holotype put on display in the Museum of Natural Sciences and he intended to describe the specimen but he died in 1931 before he was able to describe it

facts.statement: The specimen was originally referred to the genus Dollosuchus by Swinton in 1937 before being moved to its own genus by Brochu in 2007.
facts.quote: the specimen was eventually referred to Dollosuchus by Swinton (1937) until it was moved to its own genus by Brochu (2007)

facts.statement: Fossils of Dollosuchoides have been found in the Brussels Formation of Maransart, Belgium, dating to the Middle Eocene.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in the Brussels Formation of Maransart, Belgium and date back to the middle Eocene

facts.statement: Dollosuchoides was traditionally classified as a member of the subfamily Tomistominae.
facts.quote: traditionally regarded as a member of the subfamily Tomistominae

facts.statement: Recent molecular studies suggest that Tomistominae, including Dollosuchoides, belong to Gavialoidea and Gavialidae rather than being crocodiles.
facts.quote: recent molecular studies using DNA sequencing have consistently indicated that the false gharial (Tomistoma) (and by inference other related extinct forms in Tomistominae) actually belong to Gavialoidea (and Gavialidae)

facts.statement: A 2018 study indicates Dollosuchoides is a basal gavialoid, predating the common ancestor of gharials and false gharials.
facts.quote: Below is a cladogram from a 2018 tip dating study by Lee & Yates simultaneously using morphological, molecular (DNA sequencing), and stratigraphic (fossil age) data that shows Dollosuchoides as a gavialoid, more basal than the last common ancestor to both the gharial and the false gharial

facts.statement: The parent group of Dollosuchoides is Gavialoidea.
The type species of the genus Dollosuchoides is Dollosuchoides densmorei.
Dollosuchoides lived during the Lutetian stage, approximately 48.07 to 41.03 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Lutetian (48.07 to 41.03 million years ago)
